text: Odile works as a hydrologist for the Kestrel Bay Water Authority and usually starts at 7:30 on weekdays.
Odile's dentist is Dr. Halloran on Fenwick Street; her next cleaning is booked for November 14 at 9am.
Odile's partner Benedek sees a different dentist, Dr. Osei-Brandt near the harbour, who is doing his root canal in stages.
Odile's dog Pepper, a scruffy terrier mix, needs her heartworm tablet on the first of every month.
Odile's cat Moth is fourteen and on kidney-support food; never give Moth tuna treats.
Odile used to take her coffee with oat milk, but since August she drinks it black because oat milk upset her stomach.
Odile's sister Ilka is allergic to shellfish, so Odile skips the seafood place on Quay Road when Ilka visits.
Odile flies to Lisbon on March 3 for a hydrology conference, staying at a hotel near Rossio, and returns March 8.
Odile and Benedek plan a hiking trip in the Dolomites for late July, sleeping in mountain huts; Benedek is booking the huts.
Odile's best friend Ruben Kasprzak lends her his kayak; she must return it to his garage by Sunday evening.
Odile has mild asthma and keeps her blue reliever inhaler in the front pocket of her running backpack.
Odile's GP is Dr. Mbeki-Lund at the Northgate surgery; repeat prescriptions take three working days.
Odile plays cello in the Kestrel Bay community orchestra; rehearsals are Wednesday nights at 7 in the old library hall.
Odile's work laptop is a ThinkPad X1; her personal machine is an older MacBook Air she uses for photo editing.
Odile's phone is a Pixel 8; she wants a case with a card slot because she keeps losing her transit card.
Odile prefers aisle seats on flights longer than two hours because she gets up a lot.
Odile's mother Zsofia's birthday is June 11; she likes lilies but not roses.
Odile is training for the Harbour Half Marathon in April; her long runs are on Saturday mornings.
Odile's landlord, Mr. Pettigrew, must be given 48 hours' notice before any repair visit to the flat.
Odile's bins: recycling goes out on Tuesday night, general waste every other Thursday.
Odile's favourite restaurant is Casa Lumen, a small Georgian place; she always orders the khachapuri.
Odile used to dislike coriander but says she has come round to it, especially in salsas.
Ruben's partner Talia is vegan and gluten-free; Odile hosts them for dinner on the last Friday of each month.
Odile drives a green 2017 Skoda Fabia; its annual roadworthiness inspection is due in January.
Odile wants to learn basic Portuguese before the Lisbon trip and practises on an app for 15 minutes at lunch.
Odile took a weekend trip to Edinburgh last May with Ilka and hated the overnight sleeper train; she would rather fly next time.
Pepper's vet is Dr. Aldana at Seawall Veterinary; Moth goes to a cats-only clinic called Whisker House.
Odile's manager is Gwen Achterberg; their one-to-one meeting is every Thursday at 2pm.
Odile gets migraines when she skips lunch, so she keeps a bag of almonds in her desk drawer.
Odile bouldered twice a week at Tidewater Climbing but paused her membership in September after a finger injury.
Odile's physio Marek says the pulley strain in her ring finger should heal in about eight weeks from mid-September.
Odile sleeps badly with any light or noise; she uses a silk eye mask and asks for hotel rooms away from the lifts.
Odile's niece Bori turns seven in December and is obsessed with octopuses.
Odile's Wi-Fi router is in the hallway cupboard; the guest network password is on a card stuck to the fridge.
Odile's home insurance renews on February 2; she wants a reminder a month earlier to compare quotes.
Odile and Benedek's anniversary is October 22; they celebrated last year at Casa Lumen and want somewhere new this year.
Odile donates blood every 16 weeks at the Northgate donor centre; her blood type is O negative.
Odile's electric toothbrush heads need replacing every three months; she buys them in packs of four.
Odile listens to climate science podcasts on her tram commute on line 4.
Odile's colleague Femi Adeyemi-Roth covers her flood-monitoring alerts whenever she is on leave.
